pages.title: Demo App product overview
lines: # Demo App product overview
Demo App is an invented, customer-facing reporting application used to make an
Agent Studio demonstration concrete. It exists only as pinned demo data. It has
no customers, no deployment, and no relationship to any real product.
## Purpose of this Wiki
The seven pages under Demo App are the working knowledge a delivery team would
keep next to its board: the domain vocabulary, the system boundaries, the quality
bar, the release gates, one policy still under discussion, and the index of the
decision documents. Every board card in this instance is written against them.
## What the product does
| Capability | Owner surface | State in this demo |
| Saved report views | Board and report list | Backlog, card `DEMO-1` |
| Reusable dashboard filters | Dashboard | Shaping, Dossier `DEMO-W1` |
| CSV export of a report | Report detail | Human review, card `DEMO-5` |
| Export progress in the activity feed | Activity feed | In progress, card `DEMO-12` |
| Keyboard shortcuts on the board | Board | Completed, Dossier `DEMO-W5` |
## What the product deliberately does not do
- It does not schedule or email reports. Delivery is pull-only.
- It does not store report results longer than the retention policy allows; the
window itself is still open in [Export retention policy](product/export-retention-policy.md).
- It does not manage identities. Access comes from the surrounding platform.
## Where to go next
- [Reporting domain](product/reporting-domain.md) for the shared vocabulary.
- [System map](system/system-map.md) for the surfaces and their boundaries.
- [Accessibility baseline](quality/accessibility-baseline.md) for the fixed quality bar.
- [Release checklist](operations/release-checklist.md) for what has to pass before a change ships.
- [Dossier index](dossiers/README.md) for the decision record.

pages.title: Reporting domain
lines: # Reporting domain
One vocabulary for every card, Dossier, and review note in Demo App. When a term
here and a term on a card disagree, this page wins and the card is corrected.
## Terms
| Term | Means | Does not mean |
| Report | A named, parameterized query over the reporting store. | A rendered file. |
| Run | One execution of a report with concrete parameters. | A schedule. |
| Result | The rows a run produced, retained for a bounded window. | A permanent record. |
| View | A saved combination of report, parameters, and column layout. | A copy of the data. |
| Filter | A reusable parameter set that can be applied to several views. | A view. |
| Export | A file generated from one result, currently CSV only. | A run. |
## How the terms compose
Report --(parameters)--> Run --(rows)--> Result --(format)--> Export
+---------- View (report + filter) <-----+
A View never owns rows. It owns the question. That is why deleting a Result
under the retention window never deletes a View, and why the retention decision
in [Export retention policy](export-retention-policy.md) is bounded to Results
and Exports.
## Invariants
1. A Run is immutable once it has produced a Result.
2. An Export is derived; it is never the record of truth.
3. A Filter is shared. Editing it changes every View that references it, which is
the open shaping question in Dossier `DEMO-W1`.
4. Column order is part of the View, not of the Report.
## Cards that use this page
- `DEMO-1` saved views, `DEMO-10` reusable dashboard filters, `DEMO-16` export presets.
- `DEMO-5` CSV export and `DEMO-15` report sorting.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Export retention policy
lines: # Export retention policy
Draft policy for how long a Result and its Exports remain readable. The window is
**not decided**. The comparison, the recommendation, and the two open decisions
live in Dossier [Export retention and privacy](../dossiers/export-retention-and-privacy/index.html).
## Why a policy is needed
Results are cheap to produce and expensive to keep. A demo tenant produces about
1,400 runs per week; the median Result is 2.1 MB and the widest is 46 MB. Without
a window the reporting store grows without a ceiling, and every retained Export is
a copy of customer data that nobody asked to keep.
## Candidate windows
| Window | Store after 12 weeks | Recovery of a deleted Export | Privacy exposure |
| 7 days | 0.9 TB | Re-run only | Lowest |
| 30 days | 3.8 TB | Re-run, or restore within the window | Moderate |
| 90 days | 11.4 TB | Restore for a full quarter | Highest |
## Current draft rules
1. Retention applies to Results and Exports, never to Views or Filters.
2. Deletion is per Result. A partially deleted Result is not a valid state.
3. A deletion leaves a receipt so that a later question can be answered without
restoring the data. Whether that receipt is required is one of the two open
decisions.
4. Nothing in this policy grants access. Access stays with the platform.
## Related work
- Card `DEMO-17` carries this policy through preparation.
- The [release checklist](../operations/release-checklist.md) gate 7 refuses any
reporting change that widens retention before this policy is decided.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: System map
lines: # System map
The four surfaces of Demo App and the two boundaries that carry the whole export
story. Everything below is invented for the demo.
## Surfaces and boundaries
Browser client                Reporting API              Reporting store
| Board        | ------> | /reports  /runs     | ----> | reports        |
| Dashboard    |         | /results  /exports  |       | runs, results  |
| Report list  | <------ | activity stream     | <---- | export_files   |
| catalog lookups only
v
Demo Platform service
## Boundary rules
| Boundary | Rule | Enforced by |
| Client to API | No client may compose SQL. Parameters are named and typed. | API request contract |
| API to store | A Run writes exactly one Result row set and never updates it. | Store constraint |
| API to Demo Platform | Catalog lookups only. No report data crosses this edge. | Read-only credential |
| Export path | An Export is produced from a stored Result, never from a live query. | Export service |
## The export path in detail
1. The client requests an Export for one Result.
2. The export service streams the stored rows through the CSV writer.
3. Escaping and timezone formatting are applied once, in the writer.
4. Progress events reach the activity feed as they are produced, which is the work
tracked by card `DEMO-12`.
5. The finished file falls under the window described in
[Export retention policy](../product/export-retention-policy.md).
## Known structural gaps
- The empty-Result case reaches the CSV writer without an explicit assertion. This
is the single open finding on the escalated release decision, card `DEMO-9`.
- Column order is derived from the View at export time, so a reordered View
changes future Exports. That is intended, and it is why sorting is pinned in
card `DEMO-15`.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Accessibility baseline
lines: # Accessibility baseline
The fixed bar every reporting surface must clear before it reaches human review.
The baseline is a gate, not an aspiration: a surface that fails it is returned,
not annotated.
## The bar
| Check | Requirement | How it is proven |
| Contrast | 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for meaningful non-text, in both themes. | Automated scan plus a light and dark capture |
| Keyboard | Every action reachable and escapable without a pointer. | Recorded traversal of the surface |
| Focus | A visible focus ring on every interactive element. | Light and dark capture |
| Names | Every control exposes an accessible name that matches its visible label. | Automated scan |
| Status | State changes announce once, not on every repaint. | Manual review note |
| Motion | Reduced-motion honoured; no motion carries meaning alone. | Manual review note |
## Measured state of the demo surfaces
| Surface | Contrast | Keyboard | Focus | Verdict |
| Board | pass | pass | pass | Baseline met |
| Report list | pass | pass | pass | Baseline met |
| Report detail | pass | pass | pass | Baseline met |
| Export dialog | pass | pass | pass | Baseline met |
| Empty-state copy | pass | pass | pass | Copy still in review, card `DEMO-14` |
## History
The banner experiment recorded in Dossier
[Legacy notification banner experiment](../dossiers/legacy-notification-banner/index.html)
was discarded partly because it failed the status rule above: it announced on every
repaint. The keyboard shortcut map in Dossier
[Board keyboard shortcuts](../dossiers/board-keyboard-shortcuts/index.html) was
accepted because it improved the keyboard row without touching contrast.
## Cards that use this page
- `DEMO-3` updates the baseline itself.
- `DEMO-14` and `DEMO-18` are measured against it.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Release checklist
lines: # Release checklist
Nine gates. A reporting change ships when all nine pass, and it is returned as
soon as one fails. The list is deliberately short enough to be read in full
before every release.
| # | Gate | Passes when |
| 1 | Scope | The change matches one card and one Dossier direction. |
| 2 | Domain | New terms exist in [Reporting domain](../product/reporting-domain.md). |
| 3 | Boundaries | No new edge crosses the rules in [System map](../system/system-map.md). |
| 4 | Tests | Focused unit coverage exists for every changed behaviour. |
| 5 | Accessibility | The [accessibility baseline](../quality/accessibility-baseline.md) is met in both themes. |
| 6 | Evidence | A diff, a capture, and a review verdict are attached to the card. |
| 7 | Retention | Nothing widens retention while [Export retention policy](../product/export-retention-policy.md) is undecided. |
| 8 | Rollback | The change can be reverted without a data migration. |
| 9 | Decision | Any accepted risk is written down and owned. |
## Escalation
A gate that cannot be resolved inside the bounded review budget becomes an
operator decision instead of a silent pass. Card `DEMO-9` is the worked example:
gate 4 held on a missing empty-Result assertion, the automatic review budget ran
out, and the card escalated with three bounded options rather than shipping.
## Evidence expected per gate
- Gates 4 and 5 need machine-checkable output, not a claim.
- Gate 6 needs artifacts on the card, not links into a chat.
- Gate 9 needs a named owner and a fixed date; the six documents in the
[Dossier index](../dossiers/README.md) are where those land.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Dossier index
lines: # Dossier index
Six decision documents, one per lifecycle state. Together they show how a
decision is shaped, decided, delivered, documented, and discarded without any
of those states being lost.
| Key | Document | State | Reads as |
| `DEMO-W1` | [Reusable dashboard filters](reusable-dashboard-filters/index.html) | Active, shaping | Research in progress, no option chosen |
| `DEMO-W2` | [Export retention and privacy](export-retention-and-privacy/index.html) | Decision pending | Two open decisions, one recommendation |
| `DEMO-W3` | [Onboarding checklist scope](onboarding-checklist-scope/index.html) | Decided | Decided, no delivery cards yet |
| `DEMO-W4` | [Reports export release](reports-export-release/index.html) | Decided, tracking | Four live delivery points |
| `DEMO-W5` | [Board keyboard shortcuts](board-keyboard-shortcuts/index.html) | Documented | Durable documentation, every reference terminal |
| `DEMO-W6` | [Legacy notification banner experiment](legacy-notification-banner/index.html) | Archived | Discarded with a receipt |
## Reading the states
- **Active** means the document is still gathering evidence. It must not present
an option as chosen.
- **Decision pending** means the options are complete and a human owes an answer.
- **Decided** means an option was chosen and recorded. It says nothing about
delivery; `DEMO-W3` is decided with no cards, `DEMO-W4` is decided with four.
- **Documented** means the work finished and the document became the durable
record rather than a live decision.
- **Archived** means the proposal was discarded. The receipt names the actor, the
time, and the reason so the ground is never re-covered by accident.
"In implementation" is not a stored state. It is what `decided` plus non-terminal
referenced cards looks like from the board, which is exactly what `DEMO-W4` shows.
Back to the [product overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Demo Platform service overview
lines: # Demo Platform service overview
Demo Platform is an invented supporting service. It answers catalog questions for
Demo App and nothing else. It exists only as pinned demo data and is not deployed
anywhere. Every host below uses the reserved `.invalid` suffix, so no name here
can resolve.
## Responsibility
| The service does | The service does not |
| Resolve catalog entries by identifier. | Store report rows or Exports. |
| Cache catalog responses under a fixed policy. | Own identities or grant access. |
| Emit four named signals for operators. | Page anyone; this demo has no on-call. |
| Refuse writes from every caller. | Accept a fallback to a live upstream. |
## Environments in this demo
| Environment | Host | Purpose |
| Demo | `catalog.demo.invalid` | The only environment that exists here |
| Replay | `catalog.replay.invalid` | Serves the recorded fixture responses |
## Where to go next
- [Request lifecycle](concepts/request-lifecycle.md) for the seven stages.
- [Cache policy](concepts/cache-policy.md) for what is kept and for how long.
- [Observability guide](operations/observability-guide.md) for the four signals.
- [Incident checklist](operations/incident-checklist.md) for the six response steps.
- [Demo security boundary](system/demo-security-boundary.md) for what this instance cannot do.

pages.title: Request lifecycle
lines: # Request lifecycle
One catalog request, seven stages. Each stage has one job and one failure mode,
which is what makes the [incident checklist](../operations/incident-checklist.md)
short enough to be useful.
1 accept -> 2 validate -> 3 authorize -> 4 cache lookup
hit      miss
|        v
|   5 resolve
+--> 6 shape -> 7 emit
## Stages
| # | Stage | Job | Failure mode |
| 1 | Accept | Bound the body and the request rate. | Oversized or excessive request |
| 2 | Validate | Reject anything that is not a known identifier shape. | Malformed identifier |
| 3 | Authorize | Confirm the caller may read the catalog. | Unknown or read-denied caller |
| 4 | Cache lookup | Answer from the cache when the entry is fresh. | Stale entry served |
| 5 | Resolve | Read the catalog record on a miss. | Upstream unavailable |
| 6 | Shape | Produce the response contract. | Contract drift |
| 7 | Emit | Write the four signals and return. | Signal gap |
## Rules
1. Stage 3 never falls back. A caller that cannot be authorized is refused.
2. Stage 5 is the only stage allowed to touch the catalog record.
3. Stage 7 runs on every path, including refusals, so a refused request is still
visible in the [observability guide](../operations/observability-guide.md) signals.
4. No stage retries on behalf of the caller. Retry is the caller's decision.
## Cards that use this page
- `PLAT-1` adds the health-check endpoint that reports stage readiness.
- `PLAT-2` adds structured request logging across all seven stages.
Back to the [service overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Cache policy
lines: # Cache policy
What the catalog caches, for how long, and what it refuses to cache. The policy is
deliberately boring: a cache that needs judgement to reason about is a cache that
causes incidents.
## Policy
| Entry | Time to live | Refreshed by | Cached on refusal |
| Catalog entry | 10 minutes | Next read after expiry | No |
| Catalog listing | 2 minutes | Next read after expiry | No |
| Not-found result | 30 seconds | Next read after expiry | Yes, negative entry |
| Authorization outcome | Never cached | Not applicable | No |
## Rules
1. Authorization is never cached. Stage 3 of the
[request lifecycle](request-lifecycle.md) runs on every request.
2. A negative entry exists only to protect the catalog from a hot miss loop. It is
short by design.
3. The cache is per-instance and in-memory. A restart is a valid way to clear it,
which keeps the [incident checklist](../operations/incident-checklist.md) short.
4. Nothing derived from a report, a Result, or an Export is ever cached here. That
data does not cross the boundary at all.
## Measured effect in this demo
| Signal | Without cache | With cache |
| Median catalog latency | 84 ms | 11 ms |
| Catalog reads per minute | 1,240 | 190 |
| Cache hit ratio | not applicable | 0.85 |
Card `PLAT-3` delivered this policy and is completed.
Back to the [service overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Observability guide
lines: # Observability guide
Four signals, fixed names, no others. A fifth signal is a change request, not a
convenience. Names are stable so the [incident checklist](incident-checklist.md)
can reference them literally.
## The four signals
| Signal | Name | Type | Read it as |
| Traffic | `catalog.requests` | counter | Requests accepted at stage 1 |
| Errors | `catalog.refusals` | counter | Requests refused at stages 2, 3, or 5 |
| Latency | `catalog.duration` | histogram | Stage 1 to stage 7, in milliseconds |
| Saturation | `catalog.inflight` | gauge | Requests currently between stages |
## Fixed dimensions
Every signal carries exactly three dimensions: `stage`, `outcome`, and `env`.
`env` is one of `demo` or `replay`. Adding a dimension is a contract change
because dashboards and the incident checklist both depend on the shape.
## Reference values in this demo
| Signal | Steady state | Investigate above |
| `catalog.requests` | 190 per minute | 600 per minute |
| `catalog.refusals` | under 1 per minute | 10 per minute |
| `catalog.duration` p95 | 24 ms | 120 ms |
| `catalog.inflight` | 3 | 25 |
## What is deliberately absent
- No alert routes, no on-call rotation, and no notification targets. This demo
instance cannot page anyone; see [Demo security boundary](../system/demo-security-boundary.md).
- No request bodies and no caller identifiers in any signal. Only the fixed
dimensions above are recorded.
Back to the [service overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Incident checklist
lines: # Incident checklist
Six steps, in order. The goal is a written cause, not a fast silence. In this
demo instance every step is a reading step: nothing here can change a running
system.
| # | Step | Done when |
| 1 | Confirm the signal | The named signal in [Observability guide](observability-guide.md) is above its investigate line. |
| 2 | Locate the stage | The `stage` dimension names one stage of the [request lifecycle](../concepts/request-lifecycle.md). |
| 3 | Separate cause from symptom | Refusals at stage 3 and refusals at stage 5 are written down as different incidents. |
| 4 | Choose the bounded action | Restart to clear the cache, or refuse the caller, or wait. Nothing else. |
| 5 | Record the evidence | Signal values, stage, chosen action, and time are attached to the card. |
| 6 | Write the cause | One paragraph, in the past tense, with the fix or the accepted risk. |
## Bounded actions
| Situation | Action | Why it is safe |
| Stale catalog entry served | Restart the instance | The cache is in-memory and per-instance |
| Hot miss loop | Wait for the negative entry to expire | The negative entry is 30 seconds |
| Upstream unavailable at stage 5 | Refuse and record | The service never falls back |
| Unknown caller at stage 3 | Refuse and record | Authorization is never cached |
## Worked example
Card `PLAT-4` records a retried-request accounting mistake: retries were counted
twice in `catalog.requests`, which made step 1 fire on a healthy service. The card
was archived after the counting rule moved into the shape stage.
Back to the [service overview](../README.md).

pages.title: Demo security boundary
lines: # Demo security boundary
What this demo instance is, and what it is structurally unable to do. This page is
the answer to a visitor asking "is anything here real?".
## The instance is a snapshot
| Property | Value in this instance |
| Data origin | Invented fixtures, generated from a committed seed |
| Reset | The whole store is regenerated; a reseed is byte for byte identical |
| Execution | No work can be claimed, started, continued, or completed |
| Network | No outbound access from the replay path |
| Identities | No accounts, no tokens, no provider identifiers |
| Hosts | Reserved `.invalid` names only, so nothing resolves |
## What a visitor can do
- Read every board lane, card, run timeline, and evidence file.
- Read every Wiki page, and every Dossier across all six lifecycle states.
- Watch a recorded run replay that is labelled as simulated everywhere it appears.
## What a visitor cannot do
- Start, continue, review, or complete any task, from any surface, by any route.
- Change a card, a page, a Dossier, or a setting.
- Reach a repository, a credential, a secret, or a network destination.
## Why the boundary is credible
The refusal is decided by the server, not by the browser. A disabled control is a
courtesy; the denial is the contract. A caller that bypasses the client entirely
receives the same typed refusal, which is why nothing on this page depends on the
visitor behaving.
Back to the [service overview](../README.md).

items.title: Reusable dashboard filters
items.summary: Shaping document for filters that can be defined once and applied across several saved views. Records observed navigation friction, three user goals, the known constraints, and two open research questions. No option is presented as chosen.

document.lede: Filters are re-created by hand for every saved view. This document records what was observed, what a solution would have to achieve, and what is still unknown. It does not choose a direction.

blocks.html: Three directions are open. None has been chosen, and the evidence needed to choose is listed in section 04.

items.heading: A · Filter as a shared object
items.html: A Filter is created once and referenced by many Views. Editing it changes every View that references it. Strongest reuse, highest blast radius.

items.heading: B · Filter as a copyable preset
items.html: A Filter is a template. Applying it copies the parameters into the View. No blast radius, no propagation of a correction.

items.heading: C · Filter scoped to a dashboard
items.html: A Filter belongs to one dashboard and applies to its widgets only. Bounded, but does not solve reuse across the report list.

head: Direction
Reuse
Blast radius
Fits the domain page
rows: Yes, but narrower than the goal

blocks.heading: This document is still shaping
blocks.html: No direction is recommended. Choosing now would fix the blast-radius question before it has been measured, and the measurement is cheap. The next evidence step in section 04 is expected to resolve it.

blocks.text: The three goals a chosen direction must serve

items: A person who maintains eleven saved views changes one shared parameter in one place.
A person who opens somebody else's view can tell which parameters came from a Filter.
A person who breaks a Filter can see what they affected before they save it.
A Filter must never own rows. That invariant comes from the reporting domain page and is not negotiable here.
Column order stays part of the View, so a Filter cannot carry layout.
Whatever is chosen has to clear the accessibility baseline on the dashboard surface without a new pattern.

blocks.html: All figures below are invented demo measurements over a four-week pinned window.

items.title: Export retention and privacy
items.summary: Compares 7, 30, and 90-day retention for Results and Exports, records the storage, recovery, and privacy consequences of each, and recommends 30 days. The retention window and the deletion-proof requirement are both still open.

document.lede: How long a Result and its Exports stay readable, and whether a deletion has to leave a proof. Both questions are open and both are bounded.

blocks.html: Retention applies to Results and Exports only. Views and Filters are never affected, so no option below can lose a saved question.

head: Window

items.heading: Receipt per deletion
items.html: Each deleted Result leaves a small immutable record: identifier, time, and reason. Answers a later question without restoring data. Adds a durable record that itself has a retention question.

items.heading: Periodic attestation
items.html: A scheduled job asserts that nothing older than the window exists. Cheap and small, but cannot answer a question about one specific Result.

items.heading: No proof
items.html: Deletion is silent. Cheapest. A later question about one Result cannot be answered at all.

blocks.heading: Recommended: 30 days, with a receipt per deletion
blocks.html: 30 days covers the observed 21-day support window with margin while keeping the store under 4 TB. A receipt per deletion is recommended over a periodic attestation because the questions that actually arrive are about one specific Result, and an attestation cannot answer those.

blocks.html: The draft rules this document decides against live on the seeded page product/export-retention-policy.md, and gate 7 of the seeded release checklist refuses any change that widens retention while this document is open.

blocks.heading: Decision 1 · How long do Results and Exports remain readable?
blocks.html: One window applies to both Results and Exports. Views and Filters are unaffected by every option.

options.label: 7 days
options.note: Smallest store and lowest exposure. A support question older than a week needs a re-run.

options.label: 30 days (recommended)
options.note: Covers the observed 21-day support window with margin at 3.8 TB.

options.label: 90 days
options.note: Full-quarter recovery at 11.4 TB and the highest privacy exposure.

blocks.heading: Decision 2 · Must a deletion leave a proof?
blocks.html: Independent of the window. A proof answers a later question without restoring the data.

options.label: Receipt per deletion (recommended)
options.note: One immutable row per deleted Result: identifier, time, reason.

options.label: Periodic attestation
options.note: A scheduled assertion that nothing older than the window exists.

items.title: Onboarding checklist scope
items.summary: Records the chosen three-step onboarding checklist, the rejected guided-wizard alternative, the decision owner, the fixed decision time, and the acceptance boundary. The direction is decided and has deliberately not spawned implementation cards yet.

responses.comment: Three steps, no branching. The wizard is rejected for this release.

taskDraft.title: Build the three-step onboarding checklist
taskDraft.goal: Deliver a three-step onboarding checklist on the report list surface: connect a data source, open a first report, and save a first view. The checklist must be dismissible, must not block any surface, and must clear the seeded accessibility baseline in both themes.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly three steps, in the fixed order connect, open, save.
The checklist is dismissible and stays dismissed for that person.
No step blocks or overlays the report list.
Keyboard traversal and focus visibility meet the seeded accessibility baseline in both themes.
No new domain term is introduced without a matching entry on the seeded reporting-domain page.

document.lede: A three-step checklist was chosen over a guided wizard. The decision is recorded here with its owner, its time, and the boundary it accepts. No delivery card has been created from it yet.

items.heading: A · Three-step checklist (chosen)
items.html: Connect a data source, open a first report, save a first view. Dismissible, non-blocking, no branching. Three states to build and three to test.

items.heading: B · Guided wizard (rejected)
items.html: A modal flow with branching by data-source type. Higher completion on paper, but it blocks the report list, adds five states, and introduces a second navigation pattern.

head: Criterion
A · checklist
B · wizard
rows: No, the branch data model persists

blocks.heading: Decided: the three-step checklist
blocks.html: The checklist is chosen. The wizard is rejected for this release because it blocks the report list and introduces a second navigation pattern for a problem that three non-blocking steps already address.

head: Field
Value
rows: Completion stays under 40 percent for two pinned windows

items: Exactly three steps, in the order connect, open, save.
Dismissible, and it stays dismissed for that person.
It never blocks or overlays the report list.
It clears the seeded accessibility baseline in both themes.
It introduces no domain term that is missing from the seeded reporting-domain page.

blocks.heading: Decided is not delivered
blocks.html: This document is decided and has deliberately spawned no implementation cards. That is a valid resting state: the direction is fixed, the work is not scheduled. The board shows no live delivery points for this document.

items.title: Reports export release
items.summary: The chosen implementation direction for the CSV export of a report, its slice boundaries, evidence links, and review criteria. The current-state note below is written by hand and is separate from the live card points the host projects from the referenced cards.

responses.comment: CSV only for this release. A second format is a separate decision.

taskDraft.title: Deliver the reports export release
taskDraft.goal: Deliver the CSV export of a stored Result in four bounded slices: stream progress into the activity feed, verify dependency license notices, review the empty-state copy, and pin report sorting so an export is reproducible.
acceptanceCriteria: An Export is produced from a stored Result, never from a live query.
Escaping and timezone formatting happen once, inside the CSV writer.
Export progress reaches the activity feed while the file is produced.
Report sorting survives a refresh so two exports of one Result match.
Every slice attaches a diff, a capture, and a review verdict to its card.
taskDraft.chosenOption: CSV only, produced from a stored Result

document.lede: CSV export of a stored Result, delivered in four bounded slices. This document carries the direction and the review criteria; the board carries the live state.

items.heading: A · Export from a stored Result (chosen)
items.html: The export service streams rows that already exist. Reproducible, bounded, and it cannot put load on the reporting store at export time.

items.heading: B · Export from a live query
items.html: Re-run the report at export time. Always current, but two exports of the same Result can differ, and export load lands on the store.

items.heading: C · Export from a client-side buffer
items.html: The browser writes the file from what it has rendered. No server work, but the file is limited by what was fetched and escaping moves into the client.

head: Criterion
A · stored Result
B · live query
C · client buffer
rows: Two exports of one Result match

blocks.heading: Decided: CSV export from a stored Result
blocks.html: An Export is derived from a stored Result and never from a live query. Escaping and timezone formatting are applied once, inside the CSV writer. CSV is the only format in this release; a second format is a separate decision.

items.title: Board keyboard shortcuts
items.summary: The original decision, the implementation summary, the final shortcut map, the accessibility proof, the measured outcome, and the reason this document stopped being a live decision and became durable documentation.

responses.comment: Board surface only. No global shortcuts in this release.

taskDraft.title: Introduce board keyboard shortcuts
taskDraft.goal: Add a small, discoverable set of board keyboard shortcuts that never override a browser or assistive-technology binding, and prove the result against the seeded accessibility baseline in both themes.
acceptanceCriteria: Six shortcuts at most, scoped to the board surface only.
No shortcut overrides a browser or assistive-technology binding.
A discoverable help overlay lists every shortcut.
Focus stays visible after every shortcut, in both themes.
taskDraft.chosenOption: Board-scoped shortcuts with a help overlay

document.lede: Board-scoped keyboard shortcuts were decided, delivered, measured, and closed. This document is now the durable record of that work rather than an open question.

blocks.html: The original comparison is preserved unchanged so that a future proposal has to argue against what was actually weighed.

items.heading: A · Board-scoped shortcuts (chosen)
items.html: A small set active only on the board surface, with a discoverable help overlay. No conflict with browser or assistive-technology bindings.

items.heading: B · Global shortcuts (rejected)
items.html: Active on every surface. Larger benefit, but it collides with assistive-technology bindings and needs a per-surface exception list.

items.heading: C · Configurable shortcuts (rejected)
items.html: Each person defines their own. Maximum fit, but it makes the help overlay, the documentation, and every support answer person-specific.

blocks.heading: Decided and delivered: board-scoped shortcuts
blocks.html: Six shortcuts, board surface only, with a help overlay reachable from the board itself. Delivered by card DEMO-7 and completed.

The help overlay is generated from the same map that drives the handler, so the two cannot drift.
Focus movement uses the existing roving tabindex; no new focus model was introduced.

items.title: Legacy notification banner experiment
items.summary: Explains why the notification banner proposal was discarded: it duplicated the activity feed, it performed poorly in the accessibility review, and it was superseded by an inline status pattern. The archive receipt records the actor, the fixed time, and the reason.

decision.reason: Discarded: the banner duplicated the activity feed, failed the announcement rule of the accessibility baseline by re-announcing on every repaint, and was superseded by the inline status pattern already used on the report detail surface.

responses.comment: Discard. The inline status pattern already covers the need.

document.lede: A persistent notification banner above the board was proposed, prototyped, and discarded. This document exists so the same ground is not covered again by accident.

items.heading: A · Persistent banner (discarded)
items.html: A dismissible strip above the board carrying the most recent system notice. Always visible, one notice at a time.

items.heading: B · Inline status on the affected surface (superseded it)
items.html: The notice appears where the affected object is, using the pattern already present on the report detail surface. Nothing global, nothing persistent.

items.heading: C · Do nothing
items.html: The activity feed already carries every notice in order. Zero cost, and it was the honest baseline the banner had to beat.

head: Criterion
A · banner
B · inline
C · nothing
rows: Vertical space cost on the board

blocks.heading: Discarded
blocks.html: The banner was discarded. It duplicated content the activity feed already ordered correctly, it failed the announcement rule of the accessibility baseline, and the inline status pattern covered the same need without a new global surface.

head: Field
Value
rows: Demo product lead, on the accessibility reviewer's finding
Duplicated the activity feed, failed the announcement rule, superseded by the inline status pattern

blocks.heading: Archived is not completed
blocks.html: Nothing here shipped. This document is kept so that a later proposal for a global banner starts from the recorded reasons rather than re-running the same prototype.

head: Finding
Source
Severity
rows: Re-announced the same notice on every board repaint
87 percent of banner notices already existed in the activity feed

items.title: The banner failed the announcement rule
items.note: It re-announced on every repaint, which the seeded accessibility baseline lists as a blocking failure.

items.title: The content was already ordered elsewhere
items.note: 87 percent of prototype notices were duplicates of activity feed entries.

items.title: Dismissal was reflexive, not informed
items.note: A 1.8 second median dismissal is shorter than the time to read the notice. This is an inference from the timing, not a survey.

blocks.heading: None
blocks.html: The proposal is closed. If a global notice surface is proposed again, it has to answer the three findings above before a prototype is built.
